construct: real <table> markup: thead/tbody row GROUPS, whose UA display is `table-header-group` / `table-row-group` - a formatting context with no box of its own
why: `display: table` on a div is already pinned REFUSED (display-out-of-vocab). This case is the OTHER half of the same archetype and the one every real data table actually ships: the row-group wrappers the UA stylesheet creates, which are neither `table` nor any display value in the carried vocabulary. A data table cannot be proven without knowing what happens to thead/tbody, and the answer must be a NAME, because a row group that is silently flattened takes the header/body distinction with it.

canvas.note: AutoLayout has no table formatting context and no row-group concept

mustHave: if the case is refused, the refusal names the table/row-group construct in LEDGER.md
nothing is emitted that claims to be a table but has lost the header/body distinction
a grader reading the receipt can tell WHICH construct was refused, not merely that something was

predictedWall.status: PROPOSED - the receipt NAME 'table-lowering' exists in LEDGER.md but carries no FC-* code
predictedWall.why: display-out-of-vocab pins `display: table` as REFUSED by the name 'table-lowering'. That name is a LEDGER string, not a coded wall, and it was authored against a div root carrying `display: table` - not against the UA-generated `table-header-group` / `table-row-group` boxes that real <table> markup creates. I predict the row groups are flattened rather than refused, because they are ordinary boxes as far as the element walk is concerned and only their `display` value is out of vocabulary. If the refusal does fire under the name 'table-lowering' the case passes; if the groups are flattened silently, that is a SILENT-LOSS and this proposed code is what should name it. This matters beyond tables: examples/day-picker/README.md §5.3 records that react-day-picker's own `rdp-month_grid` IS a <table>, so the calendar archetype inherits whatever answer this case gets.
